title: Faith Adds New Charms to Earthly Bliss
description: Faith Adds New Charms to Earthly Bliss in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 375 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Power of Faith”, where the book credits them to the Salisbury Collection.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Faith adds new charms to earth-ly bliss, And saves us from its snares; Its aid in ev-ery du-ty brings, And soft-ens all our cares.

lines: Faith adds new charms to earthly bliss,
And saves us from its snares;
Its aid in every duty brings,
The wounded conscience knows its power
That balm the saddest heart can cheer,
And bids us seek our portion there,
Nor bids us seek in vain.
On that bright prospect may we rest,
And then, on faith's triumphant wings,

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
